title: Power vs. Endurance: Sprint vs. Distance Swimmers
text:
Physical Trade-offs in the Pool
Freestyle events demand fundamentally different physical profiles depending on race distance:

Sprinters (50m & 100m) rely on explosive power and upper-body leverage to overcome water resistance over short distances. As seen above, medalists and competitors in sprint events are both taller and noticeably heavier.
Distance swimmers (400m to 1,500m) prioritize aerobic capacity and swimming efficiency. Carrying excess muscle mass increases drag and metabolic cost across a race lasting up to fifteen minutes, resulting in leaner, lighter body profiles.

title: About
text:
Project Scope
This project examines how physical profiles—specifically height and weight—vary among elite Olympic swimmers across different events and how these body types have evolved over time.

title: About

Data Sources

Olympic Athlete Records: Historical dataset covering 120 years of Olympic competitions (271,116 records), sourced via TidyTuesday.

title: Olympic Swimmers: Body Types Across Events and Eras
text: Across both men’s and women’s competitions since 1960, Olympic swimmers have grown taller over time, with sprinters consistently holding a height advantage over distance swimmers.
